findings.passage: “The constitutional amendment would basically be authorizing this body to do whatever it pleases,” said Rep. Robert Reives II, a Sanford Democrat.
findings.note: Quote of him in a news story reposted on his campaign site (outlet not named on the page). He speaks about the photo ID constitutional amendment, saying it leaves the legislature free to write the rules. The story also says a House committee rejected two proposals to change it, one to wait until the next year to write the photo ID rules.

findings.motion: M11 Concur (House Roll Call #801, vote 62 to 47)
findings.note: House Bill 958, An Act to Make Various Changes to the Election Laws. Ratified text (https://www.ncleg.gov/Sessions/2025/Bills/House/PDF/H958v9.pdf) requires county boards to process a registration only if it states the applicant is a US citizen, with a 30-day notice and sworn statement when the question is blank (new G.S. 163-83). It also sets up routine monthly driver-license data sharing for list maintenance, cross-state data checks, and a process to remove voters flagged as possible non-citizens from a federal database. The roll call lists Reives among the No votes. The bill page (https://www.ncleg.gov/BillLookUp/2025/H958) shows the bill as vetoed by the Governor.
NC House, Third Reading (roll call #810), 2024-12-11: nay (tally 73–45); census gate: none.
subjects: photo ID for all voters (constitutional amendment, in person and by mail)

findings.passage: “This legislation is yet another example of Republican leadership making it harder for North Carolinians to vote. It opens the door for voter intimidation at polling places, completely undermines same-day registration during early voting and makes it easier to toss out valid ballots. These changes do not improve the integrity of our elections — if anything, they erode the trust of voters.”
findings.note: Joint statement issued by Reives and the Senate minority leader on the committee substitute for Senate Bill 747, Elections Law Changes. It is about election law in general (polling places, same-day registration, ballot challenges); it does not name ID or citizenship.

findings.passage: "All they want to do is make sure that you have less power as voters and that they have more power for themselves,"
findings.note: Reives, quoted by WUNC at the governor's veto event for House Bill 958 (Election Law Changes). He describes the bill as shifting power away from voters. The quote does not mention ID or citizenship; the bill's keywords on the legislature page include citizenship and ID systems, but its text was not reviewed.
